subject: Sprintwise Acceptance Checklist + Clearance Ops for MAP
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sprintwise Acceptance Checklist + Clearance Ops for MAP

Maria —

Thanks again for the call today. As promised, I’m sending a working draft of a sprintwise acceptance checklist we can operate against during the evaluation MAP (attached: olive_map_v1.xlsx). High level asks:

- We want a minimal "exit gate" per sprint (pass/fail) so we can make deterministic go/no-go decisions.
- Please confirm stakeholders who will own each acceptance test (functional owner + approver).
- We propose a 4-sprint cadence (2-week sprints) to evaluate reliability, latency, and integration surface.

Draft sprint acceptance goals (summary):
1) Sprint 1 — Integration baseline: API connectivity, auth, 95th percentile single-request latency < 600ms under test load, and successful sample inference for 10 representative prompts.
2) Sprint 2 — Quality anchors: automated concordance checks on 500 sample prompts (precision target >= 88%), end-to-end reranking smoke test.
3) Sprint 3 — Cost & scale signals: batching/throughput validation, KV cache warmup behavior, steady-state cost per 1K tokens.
4) Sprint 4 — Cutover readiness: canary roll, rollback plan validated, audit/logging verification, SOC2 evidence collection start.

Acceptance tests (attached: acceptance-testcases.md) include exact test steps, expected pass criteria, owner, and evidence location (Drive links).

Can you and Tom confirm by EOD Tuesday which of the above you want to keep, and who will be the approver for each sprint gate? If you prefer, we can convert each sprint gate into a short checklist item in your procurement packet so it lines up with your legal review.

Next steps (from our side):
- Marcus will produce a runnable test harness we can run against your staging endpoint by Wed.
- Karthik will propose rollback triggers and escalation path.
- I’ll collate MAP artifacts and update the mutual action plan to include the sprintwise exit gates.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: olive_map_v1.xlsx, acceptance-testcases.md
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@olivehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Richards <tom.richards@olivehealth.com>, Olive Health Procurement <procurement@olivehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprintwise Acceptance Checklist + Clearance Ops for MAP

Hi Naomi —

Thanks — this looks thorough and practical. Quick clarifications from our side:

- For Sprint 2 quality anchors, our clinical reviewer (Tom) wants to add a small blind set (n=200) drawn from real anonymized cases; we’ll need the concordance harness to accept that as an input.
- For Sprint 3 cost signals, procurement will require an estimation artifact showing expected token volume per month to reconcile with committed capacity.
- We can own approver duties for Sprints 1 and 2 (Tom), but need engineering signoff (procurement will nominate an approver) for Sprints 3 and 4.

I’ll attach the procurement checklist they asked for and loop in procurement for the volume estimate. Expect a follow-up with availability for a quick alignment call Wed morning.

Thanks,
Maria
Director, Digital Clinical Ops — Olive Health
maria.gomez@olivehealth.com

Attachments: OH_procurement_checklist.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@olivehealth.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprintwise Acceptance Checklist + Clearance Ops for MAP

Maria / team —

Appreciate the quick review. I attached a compact test harness README and a proposed sprint checklist snapshot below (I’ll push runnable scripts to the Drive link after we validate endpoints):

--- Proposed Sprint Acceptance Checklist (short form) ---
Sprint 1 (Integration baseline) — Owner: Olive Eng (Tom) / Assignee: Naomi
- Endpoint reachability (3 consecutive successful runs) — evidence: test-run-001.json
- Auth & token rotation test — evidence: token-rotation.log
- Latency smoke (95p < 600ms) under 50 concurrent virtual users — evidence: latency-summary.csv

Sprint 2 (Quality anchors) — Owner: Tom / Approver: Maria
- Concordance test vs blind set (n=200) — expected precision >= 88% — evidence: concordance-report.pdf
- Top-1 hallucination check on 50 red-team prompts — expected fail-rate < 2%

Sprint 3 (Cost & scale) — Owner: Olive Procurement / Approver: Olive Eng
- Batching throughput test (100 seq length, 4x batch) — target tokens/sec >= 1200
- KV cache hit-rate measurement — target >= 80% after warmup
- Cost projection doc produced for 3 scenarios (low/med/high)

Sprint 4 (Cutover readiness) — Owner: Redwood Ops / Approver: Olive Eng
- Canary deployment validated (canary to 5% of traffic) and rollback executed
- Audit log completeness check (S3/Drive evidence)
- SOC2 evidence checklist started

Attachments I uploaded: small-harness-readme.md (drive), sprint-checklist-compact.md

Notes on rollback triggers (preview):
- If concordance drops > 6% absolute vs baseline during canary, auto-fallback to previous model variant.
- If 95p latency > 1s for > 10% of canary requests, immediate rollback.

I’ll have the runnable harness and the initial load script by Wed morning so you can run the Sprint 1 suite. Naomi — I left a few TODOs in the acceptance-testcases.md for parameter thresholds; we can iterate.

— Marcus
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@olivehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprintwise Acceptance Checklist + Clearance Ops for MAP

Folks —

This looks good to lock in. A few operational clarifications before we finalize the MAP into a mutual action plan:

1) Decision window: each sprint gate will have a 48-hour decision window after evidence upload. If no decision is recorded in that window, default is to escalate to a joint ops review (Redwood + Olive) and the sprint is extended one working week.

2) Canaries & rollback: we will provide a one-click rollback in the canary control plane (documented). The triggers Marcus listed will be codified as runbook thresholds; we’ll also include a manual "safety stop" for your on-call.

3) Procurement & billing: Naomi — please prepare a conservative monthly token volume estimate and three cost scenarios (best/likely/worst) for procurement. We need that in the MAP package so Olive Procurement can align with legal and budget cycles.

4) Evidence retention: Redwood will retain test artifacts for 90 days by default; for SOC2 evidence we can extend retention to 12 months upon request (this requires an SSO/KMS addendum).

Action items before Wed alignment call:
- Maria/Tom: confirm approvers for each sprint gate (Sprints 1–4).
- Naomi: share conservative token volume numbers and attach to MAP.
- Marcus: upload harness + load script.
- Karthik: draft runbook snippets for rollback and the 48-hour decision workflow.

If you’re all aligned I’ll convert this into a MAP table and send the mutual action plan PDF for signature.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
